title: StorageAdapter port + Supabase Storage attachments backend with signed-URL upload/download
objective: Implement the swappable StorageAdapter port with SupabaseStorageAdapter as default (private bucket, tenant-prefixed keys) and the attachment endpoints using the approved signed-URL envelope flow: authorize -> validate (type allow-list, per-tenant size cap) -> record metadata + audit -> issue short-lived signed upload/download URLs; soft remove preserved (A-6, A-7, Q-22, P-09).
scope: lib/storage: StorageAdapter interface (put, get, delete, createSignedUploadUrl, createSignedDownloadUrl, exists as applicable); SupabaseStorageAdapter (server-side supabase-js Storage, service-role); FakeStorageAdapter for unit tests; adapter selected via config
Private bucket provisioning (migration or config) with no public access; tenant-prefixed object keys

Attachment endpoints per reference paths, adapted to the signed-URL envelope (the ONE documented API-contract deviation besides intake auth): request-upload (validates type PNG/JPG/PDF/DOC/DOCX + size <= per-tenant cap default 10MB, records quote_attachments metadata, returns signed upload URL + confirm token), confirm-upload (verifies object exists; post-upload verification step for magic-number concern — implement or explicitly flag per R-8), download (authorizes, returns short-lived signed download URL with attachment disposition), remove (soft, audited)
Audit add/remove; metadata in quote_attachments with storage_key
out_of_scope: Non-Supabase adapters beyond the fake (config seam only)
Export storage (not in scope per Q-18)
implementation_details: Bucket policies: storage access is server-only (service-role via adapter); signed URLs are the exclusive client path; RLS/storage policies deny anon access (spec 16).

Signed upload URL: Supabase createSignedUploadUrl; enforce size at validation time and verify object size/content-type on confirm (HEAD/metadata) since direct-to-storage bypasses the function body limit (A-7); reject + clean up on mismatch.

Magic-number verification: attempt lightweight post-upload check (download first bytes server-side) — if infeasible within limits, raise an explicit accepted-risk finding rather than dropping silently (spec 5 implementation note, R-8).
Per-tenant cap read from business rules (T-020); closed-quote attachment rules per reference behavior.
Document the envelope DTO as a contract deviation (M-07) in the API notes.

unit: Type allow-list + size validation rules; key-scheme generation/sanitization; FakeStorageAdapter contract tests shared with the real adapter (adapter conformance suite)
integration: Against local Supabase Storage: request-upload -> PUT bytes to signed URL -> confirm records/verifies; oversize and disallowed type rejected before signing; size/content-type mismatch on confirm rejected + object cleaned
Download returns working short-lived signed URL, authorized + tenant-isolated (cross-tenant attachment 404); soft remove hides but preserves; audit rows on add/remove
Anon key cannot read the bucket directly
e2e: Attachment upload/download via UI in T-043 (after T-028)

findings.summary: Magic-number validation moved from mid-stream to a post-upload confirm step (R-8): hostile bytes transiently exist in the private bucket before rejection.
findings.detail: IMPLEMENTED, not dropped: confirm reads the object's leading 8 bytes via a ranged read and rejects a mismatch with ATTACHMENT_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH, deleting both the object and the pending row. What differs from the .NET reference is TIMING, not coverage. The reference inspected bytes as they streamed THROUGH the API, so a mismatched file never reached storage; under A-7/Q-22 the client transfers directly to Storage, so the check necessarily runs AFTER the object lands. Residual exposure: a hostile object exists in the bucket between transfer and confirm. It is unreachable during that window (private bucket, zero storage RLS policies, and no signed URL is ever minted for an unconfirmed attachment), and it is deleted on rejection. Also preserved verbatim from the reference: DOCX cannot be distinguished from any other ZIP-family file at the header level. Tested in attachments.test.ts (PNG-as-PDF and MZ-as-PDF both rejected and cleaned up) and attachment-content.test.ts.

findings.summary: Unconfirmed attachments whose upload is abandoned leave an orphaned storage object; no reaper is implemented.
findings.detail: A caller can request an upload envelope, transfer bytes, and never call confirm. The pending row is invisible to every read path (the live-set predicate requires confirmed_at is not null) and no signed download URL can be issued for it, so it is not a data-exposure issue - but the object and its row accumulate. Reaping is deliberately NOT implemented here: it is a scheduled-job concern and this task owns no cron surface. Recommend a follow-up cron handler deleting objects+rows where confirmed_at is null and uploaded_at is older than the Supabase upload-token TTL (2h), which is idempotent and retry-safe. Raised explicitly rather than left silent. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-20): verified — the pending row is invisible to list and download (constructed: an unconfirmed attachment 404s on download and is absent from the list; re-applying the M7 mutant that drops confirmed_at from the live-set predicate fails exactly that test), so this is hygiene, not exposure. RULING: a follow-up cron task IS warranted (CLAUDE.md lists 'clean up expired transient data' as a standard job; the deletion is idempotent and retry-safe by construction: object first, then row, keyed on confirmed_at is null and uploaded_at older than the 2h token TTL). KEPT OPEN as a routing finding for the orchestrator to scope the reaper task; not a T-027 defect — this task owns no cron surface.

findings.summary: Signed UPLOAD URL lifetime is fixed at 2h by Supabase Storage and cannot be shortened through the client API.
findings.detail: MEASURED against @supabase/storage-js 2.110.7: createSignedUploadUrl(path, {upsert}) accepts no expiresIn; the TTL is set server-side. The adapter REPORTS that value (SUPABASE_UPLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 7200) rather than pretending to choose it, so the envelope's expiresInSeconds is honest. DOWNLOAD expiry IS caller-chosen, is set to 300s, and its enforcement is tested against the real service. Mitigations for the long upload TTL: the token authorizes writing exactly ONE server-chosen key already bound to one tenant and one quote; upsert is left false so a token cannot replace an already-confirmed object; and an unconfirmed object is never readable through the product. An S3/MinIO adapter could choose a shorter upload TTL with no domain-code change. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-20): the measured claim is verified against the installed @supabase/storage-js 2.110.7 type declarations — createSignedUploadUrl(path, options?: {upsert: boolean}) accepts no expiresIn. The mitigations are verified in code and test: the token targets ONE server-chosen key whose metadata row already binds tenant and quote; upsert is left false (the adapter passes no options), so a retained token cannot replace a confirmed, signature-checked object — a real TOCTOU defence, documented in the adapter header; and an unconfirmed object is unreachable through the product. Residual risk ACCEPTED: possession of the 2h token allows writing only an object that can never be read until it passes confirm-time verification. Route a note to the T-044 deviation/risk ledger. RESOLVED.

findings.summary: Storage-level bucket size backstop is 25 MiB; a tenant max_attachment_mb above that would be silently unusable.
findings.detail: max_attachment_mb has no enforced upper bound in the business-rules validator (only > 0), while the bucket carries file_size_limit = 26214400 as defence in depth. A tenant cap above 25 MB would pass the server's per-tenant check, issue a signed URL, and then be refused by Storage at transfer time with an error the product does not translate. The 25 MiB figure matches the reference's own documented ceiling (AttachmentEndpoints MaxSupportedTenantCapMb = 20 plus its 25% multipart headroom). Flagged rather than assumed away; raise both in lockstep if such a cap is ever permitted. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-20): verified, and one material fact ADDED — the trap is REFERENCE PARITY, not introduced here. UpdateBusinessRulesValidator.cs:27 is also GreaterThan(0) with no upper bound, and AttachmentEndpoints.cs:26-37 documents the same ceiling (MaxSupportedTenantCapMb = 20 + 25% headroom, below Kestrel's ~28.6 MB), so a reference tenant setting a 50 MB cap hit the identical silent refusal at the transport layer. The port preserves the measured contract exactly; tightening the business-rules validator would be a T-020-surface contract change (previously-accepted values would begin to 422) needing its own criterion. WONT_FIX in T-027; recorded so that any future task permitting caps above 25 MB must raise the bucket file_size_limit and add the validator bound in lockstep (the migration comment says the same). Noted for the T-044 ledger.

findings.summary: Reference contradictions recorded: key scheme, absent list endpoint, and routes/columns with no .NET counterpart.
findings.detail: (1) KEY SCHEME. The task file specifies {tenantId}/{leadId}/{quoteId}/{attachmentId}-{name}; the reference (AttachmentStorageKey.BuildKey) uses t{tenantId}/quotes/{quoteId}/{attachmentId}_{name} - t-prefixed tenant segment, literal 'quotes' segment, NO lead segment, underscore separator. The REFERENCE scheme is implemented. (2) NO LIST ENDPOINT EXISTS IN THE REFERENCE. AttachmentEndpoints exposes only upload, download and remove, and QuoteDto carries no attachments field; the SPA compensated with component-local state that lost attachments on reload (a gap QuotesCard.tsx:128-131 documents against itself). AC-057/V-073 require removed attachments to disappear from 'the quote's list', which is unverifiable without one, so GET /quotes/{id}/attachments was ADDED (bare array, mirroring GET /leads/{id}/quotes - measured, not assumed). (3) POST /attachments/{id}/confirm has no counterpart because the reference upload was atomic; it is part of the approved M-07/A-7 deviation. (4) Two new error codes (ATTACHMENT_OBJECT_MISSING, ATTACHMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED) cover states the atomic upload could not reach. (5) A migration adds quote_attachments.confirmed_at plus a partial index; both are registered as target-only deviations in schema-business-dotnet-parity.test.ts with justifications and a side-assertion proving they exist only in the target.

findings.summary: Declared-vs-actual size mismatch within the cap is accepted, recording the server-observed size (FLAGGED decision).
findings.detail: The task file says to 'reject + clean up on mismatch' at confirm. Implemented narrower on purpose: confirm rejects when the SERVER-OBSERVED size exceeds the tenant cap (the security property) or when the magic number disagrees, and otherwise records the observed size rather than rejecting a benign declared/actual difference. Rationale: the declared size is an untrusted hint used only for the cheap pre-signing rejection, and the migration is explicit that size_bytes/content_type hold server-observed values; rejecting an in-cap mismatch would fail legitimate uploads (e.g. a client rounding a size) without adding a security property, since the cap check already bounds the real bytes. Tested: a client declaring 10 bytes and transferring 4096 is accepted with 4096 persisted; declaring 1 KB and transferring 2 MB against a 1 MB cap is rejected and cleaned up. Flagged for evaluator review rather than silently chosen. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-20): ACCEPTED. The security property is the cap on the bytes that actually arrived, which is enforced at confirm on the server-observed size (verified by test: declared-honest-but-oversize object rejected AND object deleted AND row dropped); the declared size is an untrusted pre-signing hint, and rejecting a benign in-cap mismatch would fail legitimate clients while adding no property the cap does not already provide. The persisted size is the server-observed one (verified: declared 10, transferred 4096, persisted 4096 — and mutant M6 persisting the declared size is reported killed by that test). The narrower reading of the brief is the better-engineered one. RESOLVED.

findings.summary: AC-095 deviation-ledger routing: T-044 must record the T-027 additions and residuals so the 'exactly two deviations' criterion stays honest.
findings.detail: AC-095 pins the /api/v1 surface to exactly two documented deviations (A-7 envelope, Q-19 intake auth) and requires any additional deviation to be flagged, never absorbed. T-027 produces four items for the T-044 ledger: (1) GET /quotes/{id}/attachments — an ADDED endpoint with NO reference counterpart (AttachmentEndpoints.cs exposes only upload/download/remove and QuoteDto has no attachments field), added because AC-057/V-073's 'disappears from the quote's list' is unverifiable without it. Evaluator ruling: the addition is the RIGHT call — amending AC-057 instead would have preserved a documented SPA defect (QuotesCard.tsx:128-131 loses attachments on reload); the endpoint mirrors the measured GET /leads/{id}/quotes bare-array contract, is permission-bound (quotes.view) and tenant-isolated, and its paired frontend consumer is T-028. It should be recorded either as a component of the A-7 envelope deviation or as an explicit third entry — T-044's call, but it must appear. (2) POST /attachments/{id}/confirm plus the two new error codes (ATTACHMENT_OBJECT_MISSING, ATTACHMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED) — components of the approved A-7 envelope deviation. (3) The magic-number TIMING residual (AC-095/R-8): validation is implemented and tested, but 'never written' has become 'written, then deleted' — a hostile object exists in the private bucket between transfer and confirm/abandonment, unreachable in that window (verified: private bucket, zero storage RLS policies, no signed URL for confirmed_at IS NULL rows, list excludes them). Accepted residual; belongs in the ledger. (4) The Supabase-fixed 2h upload-token TTL (F-027-3) as a documented platform constraint with its mitigations. OPEN until T-044 records them.
